title: Admin - Comment Moderation - Moderate Vendor Responses - Functional Test Plan
overview: Functional testing of the Admin Comment Moderation - Moderate Vendor Responses feature on the Y4J platform. This feature allows Admins to moderate vendor responses separately from reviews, with distinct tagging, AI moderation rules applied, independent approve/reject actions, and approved responses becoming visible under the associated review. Covers tagging, AI moderation, admin actions, visibility, and independence from review moderation.

testCases.title: Vendor responses are tagged distinctly from reviews
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Both vendor responses and reviews exist in the moderation queue.
expectedResults: Vendor responses have a distinct 'Vendor Response' type tag
The tag is visually different from 'Review' and 'Query' tags
The tag clearly identifies the content as a vendor response
Admins can easily distinguish vendor responses from reviews at a glance
testCases.postconditions: Vendor response tagging is confirmed distinct

testCases.title: AI moderation rules apply to vendor responses
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A vendor response with offensive/spam content has been submitted.
steps: Find a vendor response that was flagged by AI moderation
expectedResults: AI moderation rules (offensive language, spam detection, sentiment) apply to vendor responses
Flagged vendor responses show Device Matcher Notes
Offensive keywords are highlighted with red badges (if applicable)
The same AI rules that apply to reviews also apply to vendor responses
testCases.postconditions: AI moderation is confirmed applied to vendor responses

testCases.title: Admin can approve vendor response independently
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending vendor response exists.
steps: Find a vendor response card with pending status
expectedResults: An 'Approve' action is available on vendor response cards
Clicking Approve changes the status to 'Approved'
The approval is independent of the associated review's status
A success notification may be displayed

testCases.title: Admin can reject vendor response independently
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A pending vendor response exists.
steps: Find a vendor response card with pending status
expectedResults: A 'Reject' action is available on vendor response cards
Clicking Reject changes the status to 'Rejected'
The rejection is independent of the associated review's status
The vendor response is hidden from public view

testCases.title: Approved vendor response becomes visible under the review
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A vendor response has been approved. The associated review is also approved.
steps: Open a new browser/incognito window as a regular user
Navigate to the product page with the associated review
Observe if the vendor response appears under the review
expectedResults: The approved vendor response is visible under the associated review
The response is clearly labeled as from the vendor
The response text matches what was submitted
The response is positioned below/after the review it responds to
testCases.postconditions: Approved vendor response is publicly visible under the review

testCases.title: Rejected vendor response is NOT visible under the review
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A vendor response has been rejected.
steps: Open a new browser/incognito window as a regular user
Navigate to the product page with the associated review
Observe if the vendor response appears
expectedResults: The rejected vendor response is NOT visible to public users
Only the review is shown (without the vendor response)
No trace of the rejected response is visible to users
testCases.postconditions: Rejected vendor response is confirmed hidden

testCases.title: Vendor response moderation is independent from review moderation
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A review and its vendor response both exist in moderation.
steps: Find a review and its associated vendor response in the moderation queue
Observe the vendor response status — it should remain unchanged
Separately approve or reject the vendor response
expectedResults: Approving the review does NOT auto-approve the vendor response
The vendor response retains its own independent status
Each item must be moderated separately
Admin has full control over each piece of content independently

testCases.title: Vendor responses appear when filtering by 'Vendor Responses' type
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. Vendor responses exist in moderation.
steps: Select 'Vendor Responses' from the content type filter
expectedResults: Only vendor response cards are displayed
No reviews or queries are shown
Each card has the 'Vendor Response' type tag
The filter correctly isolates vendor responses
testCases.postconditions: Type filter works for vendor responses

testCases.title: Vendor response card shows associated product and review context
testCases.preconditions: User is logged in as Admin. A vendor response exists.
expectedResults: The card shows the vendor response text
The associated product name is displayed
The vendor's name/role is shown
Enough context is provided for the admin to make a moderation decision
testCases.postconditions: Vendor response card provides sufficient context

testCases.title: Pending vendor response is not visible to public users
testCases.preconditions: A vendor response is in pending/needs review status (not yet approved).
steps: Verify a vendor response is in pending status
Open a new browser as a regular user
Navigate to the product page with the associated review
Observe if the pending vendor response is visible
expectedResults: The pending vendor response is NOT visible to public users
Only approved vendor responses are shown publicly
The review is visible but without the pending response
Content remains hidden until admin approves
testCases.postconditions: Pending vendor responses are confirmed hidden from public
